Subject: URGENT: PeakCheckout parser traceback — exec notice

Karthik / Markus — PeakCheckout (large checkout flow) is seeing a spike in errors and tail latency. They attached a pcap and the stacktrace points to our streaming parser failing to reassemble headers correctly (HeaderParseError). Customer impact: revenue checkout failures, currently elevated error rate.

Key facts:
- Origin: hosted API (us-west)
- Seen by customer with our client SDK in their service (they claim SDK v1.4.2)
- Symptom: header alignment exceptions in parser, intermittent and more likely under high concurrency/parallel chunking

Request: please triage with urgency. Potential areas to check: SDK reassembly edge-case, server-side chunk coalescing, parser strictness. If we can reproduce, we should prepare both: (a) server-side relaxed parser as an immediate mitigation; (b) SDK patch + Hosted rollback plan.

I can coordinate customer communications and inform legal/finance about a possible SLA credit ask.

-JW

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:02:45 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: PeakCheckout parser traceback — exec notice

Triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced locally using Peak's repro script + our SDK v1.4.2 under parallel workers (50 concurrent).
- Root cause hypothesis: race in the SDK stream-reassembly buffer where two consecutive chunks that contain header terminators are coalesced incorrectly when chunk boundaries align exactly with CRLF sequences. This results in an off-by-n offset being passed into the header parser and a HeaderParseError.
- Failure mode increases with small MTU-sized chunks and concurrent connections (matches customer's load).

Planned immediate actions:
1) Deploy a server-side relaxed-parser flag in Hosted that tolerates a missing LF when contiguous header bytes are present. This is a short-lived mitigation (minutes -> hours).
2) Patch SDK to 1.4.3 with a fix for the buffer flush ordering + add unit tests. Target: patch branch created and nightly build within 4 hours.
3) Canary rollout of server-side change to 5% of PeakCheckout traffic; monitor error-rate and latency.

I'll own the engineering plan and will post status updates to JIRA-INC-4821. If we confirm SDK root cause, we'll backport to Dedicated images and prepare a Private deployment advisory.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Asha — update and immediate mitigations: 
1) We will enable a temporary server-side parser tolerance for your traffic in us-west in the next 15 minutes (canary 5%). This should stop the HeaderParseError class and bring error-rate back down while we ship the SDK fix.
2) Engineering has reproduced the issue and is preparing SDK v1.4.3 with a buffer-reassembly fix; nightly build targeted in ~4 hours.
3) You can also try a client-side workaround: set environment variable REDWOOD_STRICT_REASSEMBLY=false (we can provide the exact toggle) — this will avoid the parser throwing on borderline sequences.

We apologize for the disruption. We're treating this as P1 and will keep you updated every hour. If you want a bridge, we're available now. We'll also propose a service credit for the window of impact.
